item.title: Pentagon sends hundreds of Army troops to Latin America for training as drug-trafficking campaign expands
item.description: Troops from the 10th Mountain Division are deploying to Panama for jungle training as the Pentagon expands military operations against drug traffickers.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. military is deploying several hundred Army soldiers to Latin America for training and joint exercises with regional forces as the Trump administration expands its campaign against drug-trafficking networks, Fox News confirmed.

The deployment involves soldiers from the Army's 10th Mountain Division based at Fort Drum, New York, with the first troops from a roughly 600-soldier battalion expected to deploy to Panama, according to The New York Times, which first reported the deployment.

A senior U.S. official confirmed to Fox News that the troops are being forward-staged under U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM), which will determine where they are ultimately deployed.

According to The Times, the troops will first deploy to a new jungle training facility in Panama before eventually training with local forces in Colombia and Honduras.

EXCLUSIVE: TRUMP’S NEW SECURITY ALLIANCE FACES FIRST REAL-WORLD TEST DEEP IN SOUTH AMERICA AS TROOPS DEPLOY

The troops could also support U.S. special operations personnel who are advising local militaries conducting raids against suspected drug traffickers, the outlet reported.

Separately, several hundred soldiers from the 10th Mountain Division are expected to help staff a new Western Hemisphere military command based in Miami.

The deployment comes as the Pentagon continues military operations targeting suspected drug traffickers across Latin America and the Caribbean.

US MILITARY STRIKES ALLEGED NARCO-TRAFFICKING VESSEL IN CARIBBEAN, KILLING 4 'NARCO-TERRORISTS'

Since the campaign began more than a year ago, U.S. forces have conducted dozens of strikes, with more than 235 people killed.

Gen. Francis Donovan, commander of SOUTHCOM, previously said the military was considering operations against trafficking networks on land.

"Do I see land strikes as options? Yes. We want all options at the table," Donovan said in an interview with The Wall Street Journal.

"Those actions might be strikes, arrests, or the takedown of a safe house," he continued. "It could even be something as routine as increasing the use of cargo scanners at border checkpoints."

TRUMP ADMIN'S LIST OF US-DESIGNATED 'FOREIGN TERRORIST' GROUPS IN LATIN AMERICA EXPANDS TO 21

Donovan added that the goal was to create "total systemic friction" for the cartels.

The Trump administration has pursued agreements with allied nations that could allow it to expand military operations against trafficking networks onto land in multiple Latin American countries.

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth previously said during a visit to Panama in August that Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras had agreed to allow the U.S. to carry out joint military operations against criminal groups within their borders, although Guatemala denied reaching such an agreement.

item.title: Brewers steal Game 3 on Dodgers' home turf to go up 3-0, pushing LA to brink of elimination
item.description: Jackson Chourio's leadoff homer off Blake Snell set the tone as the Milwaukee Brewers seized a commanding 3-0 NLCS lead over the LA Dodgers.
item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers pushed the Los Angeles Dodgers to the brink of elimination Wednesday night with a 6-2 Game 3 victory at Dodger Stadium.

One win now separates Milwaukee from completing the sweep and returning the favor for last year's NLCS.

Jackson Chourio ambushed Blake Snell’s first pitch of the night for a leadoff blast, and Robert Gasser protected the lead with five shutout frames.

After the Dodgers briefly went ahead in the sixth on Will Smith’s two-run double, Milwaukee answered in three batters. Snell walked Andrew Vaughn to open the seventh before Jake Bauers won an 11-pitch battle with a go-ahead, two-run missile. Garrett Mitchell hammered the next pitch over the wall to chase Snell and make it 4-2.

A wild pitch in the eighth, a Joey Ortiz RBI single in the ninth, and 3.2 scoreless relief innings from DL Hall and Trevor Megill finished the job.

For the first time in the Shohei Ohtani era, the Dodgers look utterly spent. This series has mirrored the 2004 NBA Finals, when the Detroit Pistons dismantled the Shaq-and-Kobe Lakers through relentless collective force. There are no 2024 Tommy Edman heroics and no 2025 Ohtani masterclasses to save them.

A DODGERS-LESS WORLD SERIES WOULD HURT NOW, BUT HELP MLB LATER | BOBBY BURACK

This year, with nobody willing to sound the alarm, an exhausted lineup is simply dragging bats through the zone with so little fight that fans online have cynically wondered if LA is throwing the series to kill the sport's salary-cap debate.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts offered the only posture left for a manager running out of runway.

"You just gotta win tomorrow," Roberts said. "We've just got to get a win and find a way to build some momentum."

After the win, Bauers noted that last year's squad "flew to LA knowing we were heading to a funeral," while this group arrived fully expecting to win.

The Dodgers built what was supposed to be an indestructible machine. Milwaukee has reduced it to a team on fumes, with a chance to lower the casket Thursday night in Game 4.

item.title: Trump wishes Pope Leo speedy recovery after lung cancer diagnosis, speaks highly of pontiff's brother
item.description: President Donald Trump revealed Pope Leo XIV's brother is a friend and avid MAGA supporter with memorabilia "all over" his house while wishing the pontiff well.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump wished Pope Leo XIV a speedy recovery Wednesday following his lung cancer diagnosis, revealing that he is friends with the pontiff's brother, whom he described as an enthusiastic MAGA supporter.

Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One while traveling from Arizona to Montana, Trump expressed optimism about the 71-year-old pontiff's recovery following surgery to remove part of his right lung.

"I want to see Pope Leo get well. I hear the prognosis for that type of a problem. It's a cancer. It's big stuff. Anytime you have cancer," the president said. "But the prognosis seems to be good, I've watched. And we just want to wish him our love and our best wishes."

POPE LEO XIV BEGINS HISTORIC 4-DAY VISIT TO FRANCE

Trump then discussed his friendship with the pope's brother and his wife, describing them as enthusiastic supporters of the president.

"His brother is a friend of mine, who's a great — he's a fantastic guy — and his wife. You know, they're big Trump supporters. They have MAGA all over their house," he continued. "And I can say that his brother loves him a lot. Loves the pope a lot, and that's good, but I just want to wish him well. Get better fast."

The president's remarks came one day after the Vatican announced that Leo had been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, a form of lung cancer, following surgery at Agostino Gemelli University Hospital in Rome.

According to the Holy See Press Office, doctors removed the lower lobe of the pontiff's right lung during a procedure that lasted approximately 90 minutes. Doctors reported no complications.

TRUMP TAKES AIM AT POPE LEO XIV MEETING WITH 'USELESS' CHICAGO MAYOR BRANDON JOHNSON AT VATICAN

The Vatican said the cancer diagnosis was confirmed through an examination of tissue collected during surgery, consistent with findings from tests conducted before the procedure.

Leo had previously disclosed that doctors discovered a small lump in his lung at an early stage and recommended surgery. Following the operation, he awoke normally and returned to his hospital room after a brief observation period, according to the Vatican.

Fox News Digital's Anders Hagstrom and Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.

item.title: Tony Dungy tells Sage Steele that NBC wasn't happy with his pro-life views: 'They knew where I stood'
item.description: Tony Dungy told Sage Steele he believes his outspoken Christian faith and pro-life stance led to his departure from NBC after years as an analyst.
item.content:encoded:
Legendary NFL head coach and football analyst Tony Dungy is not going to apologize for being convicted in his religious beliefs.

Dungy spent years as an analyst on NBC, sharing his insight after a 13-year head coaching career in the NFL and a Super Bowl championship with the Indianapolis Colts. But curiously, despite his popularity and wealth of experience, Dungy and NBC parted ways in early 2026.

He told former ESPN personality Sage Steele that he had a sneaking suspicion as to why. During a recent, lengthy interview on "The Sage Steele Show", Dungy explained what he believed led to his exit and why he doesn't regret what he did.

HALL OF FAMER TONY DUNGY ENDORSES MICHELE TAFOYA IN CROWDED MINNESOTA REPUBLICAN PRIMARY FOR U.S. SENATE

Steele brought up NBC, then said from the outside, it seemed like it "was tied to you being more and more vocal about your beliefs with faith, with being pro-life."

Dungy didn't deny it, saying he felt that it wasn't always appreciated that he spoke out about his faith.

"There are some things that, I guess in TV especially, they want you to be careful because they want to attract everybody. They want to have an audience of everyone. They don’t always appreciate you speaking about your faith. But for me, I’m always going to do that. I'm going to try and do it in a respectful way, but people are going to know that I’m a Christian."

Relatedly, Dungy also spoke at the "March for Life" event, which he later told Steele was not a popular decision with the NBC brass. Steele asked Dungy if he'd asked permission before speaking, to which he confirmed he hadn't.

ESPN COLLEGE GAMEDAY 'NO RELIGIOUS SIGNS' RULE DRAWS BACKLASH DURING ALABAMA VS GEORGIA BROADCAST

"And they were not happy that I went because … their point is, ‘Hey, we’ve got audience on all sides of the spectrum. We don’t want to push away anyone just making statements like that.’ And I said, ‘Well, I get it, but this is an important topic to me. I was asked to speak and because it was important to me, I did.’"

Steele interjected, saying that he kept talking about it anyway, including making posts on social media.

"They knew where I stood. I knew where they stood… there are some things I’m not going to try to turn an audience away, but things that are important to me I’m going to talk about. If somebody asked me a question about my faith and am I a Christian, I’m not going to say no. I’m not going to shy away from it."

When Steele wondered whether he'd thought of backing off his public statements on faith and being pro-life, Dungy again said no. "I said I've got to do it in the right way, and I can't do it in a belligerent manner."

Then he makes the important distinction: "You're also not doing it on 'Sunday Night Football.' I'm not going to use that platform as, 'Oh, by the way, stop talking about the game tonight. Let me just make a point about abortion.'"

A few minutes later, Dungy admitted that he was "pretty sure" his time at the network would be coming to an end over publicly sharing his religious views.

"I was pretty sure it was. There were things that they didn't want me to talk about and we had a good understanding. They knew who I was when I got hired and, you know, it is what it is."

Though he knew it was coming, Dungy didn't go as far as saying that's definitively why he was let go. When asked directly, he said, "I don't know. And it really doesn't matter."

Another "job" Dungy lost? He was taken off the Hall of Fame voting committee. When Steele brought that up, potentially wondering if that too was related to his public comments, he said he was told it was completely unrelated, "I don't know exactly, they said that they wanted to go from 50 voters to 25. They thought it would make an easier process."

It's interesting to contrast how NBC apparently handled Dungy's public statements of faith, and how that relates to his views on abortion, with how many networks have little problem with comments supporting the political left or left-wing issues.

Does anyone really believe that NBC would have a problem if one of their football analysts appeared at a "No Kings" protest? Or a pro-choice march? Or spoke about gun control? Of course not. The concerns over political topics only ever go in one direction. Because the right is viewed as divisive by liberal corporations, and the left is viewed as empathetic common sense.

item.title: NFL says first regular-season game in France remains on track despite growing unrest in Paris
item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints are set to meet at Stade de France on Oct. 25 despite weeks of protests roiling Paris streets.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this season, the NFL sanctioned its first regular-season game in Australia, extending the league’s international reach beyond its longstanding presence in England.

The 2026-27 season is also set to feature a record number of games outside the United States. In addition to Australia and England, games will be played in France, Brazil, Spain, Germany and Mexico.

As the NFL’s inaugural game in the Paris area approaches, social unrest and protests in France have entered their third week, creating a broader security backdrop for the event. However, the league said Wednesday that the game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints is still expected to take place as scheduled Oct. 25 at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, north of Paris.

NFL OWNERS APPROVE RECORD 10 INTERNATIONAL GAMES FOR 2027 WITH SIGHTS ON MORE EXPANSION ABROAD

There is precedent for the NFL relocating games, although past changes have typically been prompted by extreme weather or field conditions.

"We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on Oct. 25," the NFL said in a statement obtained by ESPN. "As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."

ROGER GOODELL DETAILS NFL EXPANSION POSSIBILITIES AND A TIMETABLE FOR A FULL SEASON OF INTERNATIONAL GAMES

Calls for broad changes to France’s education system have been at the center of the unrest. Protesters want the government to address schools that have been considered under-resourced, as well as deteriorating facilities and teacher shortages. Some students have described buildings in disrepair and reported seeing rats inside.

Some demonstrations have escalated into violence, prompting French authorities to deploy tear gas, stun grenades and other crowd-control measures, CBS News reported.

France will hold presidential elections next spring.

The Saints will be the designated home team for the game in France. New Orleans enters its Week 6 matchup with the New York Giants on a three-game losing streak.

item.title: Parents speak out on The Ingraham Angle after girls forfeit race over biological male runner
item.description: Camas High School girls walked off a cross-country course after a transgender athlete switched from the boys' team to the girls' roster midseason.
item.content:encoded:
Roughly a dozen high school girls took their spots at the starting line of a Washington cross-country meet and walked off the course in protest. The Oct. 13 protest, reported by Fox News Digital's Jackson Thompson, at a Camas High School dual meet against Battle Ground followed a decision allowing a male athlete to switch from the boys' team to the girls' varsity roster midseason.

On Sept. 5, the athlete finished 76th in an Oregon boys' junior varsity race. Just ten days later, that same runner was competing in the girls' division, as reported by OutKick's Matt Calkins.

A CROSS COUNTRY RUNNER SWITCHED TO THE GIRLS TEAM MIDSEASON, PARENTS VOICE THEIR DISAPPROVAL AT MEET

School officials were fine rubber-stamping the decision, but the young Camas runners weren't about to pretend it was a level playing field. They walked off the course.

Parents Kevin and Sarah Burns appeared on "The Ingraham Angle" to explain why their daughter Holly and her teammates decided they had seen enough.

"Well, we told her that they should do what they feel is best and that they feel is right. And they got the support from their teammates, and they decided to make a difference," Kevin Burns said.

DAD BANNED FROM SCHOOL GROUNDS AFTER PROTESTING TRANS RUNNER COMPETING AGAINST HIS DAUGHTER

"I think if only a couple of girls had walked off it, they would have lost some opportunities. And I don't think it would have mattered so much. But so many of them," he added. "And I want you to remember that several of the girls, such as the team, team captains, had quit before this. So there really was a lot more girls than you see in the video that were protesting this."

When families questioned the runner's eligibility, the Camas School District said its hands were tied by state rules.

WASHINGTON FAMILY REQUESTS SCOTUS INJUNCTION AFTER DAUGHTER WAS ALLEGEDLY SEXUALLY ASSAULTED BY TRANS ATHLETE

Officials explained that Washington law and high school athletic regulations require schools to let athletes compete in divisions matching their gender identity.

Holly's father explained that the school's response effectively shut down the issue.

WASHINGTON OFFICIALS CALL GIRL’S CLAIMED EMERGENCY ‘MANUFACTURED’ AFTER ALLEGED TRANS ATHLETE SEXUAL ASSAULT

"The school sent us out a letter stating that, based on Washington law, it prohibits discrimination based on gender identity and expression," he said. When Ingraham summarized the letter as telling families they were out of luck, he agreed: "I guess it's okay to discriminate against actual gender."

With athletic institutions and legacy sports figures largely silent, the burden of taking a stand fell on teenagers.

I LOST A STATE CHAMPIONSHIP TO A BOY. I REFUSE TO LOSE MY VOICE

Holly's mother addressed the emotional weight placed on young competitors who simply wanted to run.

"They're children, they're, you know, they're 16 to 17-year-old girls that shouldn't have to deal with this at all, shouldn't even be on their radar," Sarah Burns said. "You know, they should just be able to go out there and race and have fun and not deal with this adult issue."

The friction carried straight onto the sidelines during the meet.

When the parents arrived with signs to support the runners, security attempted to remove them.

WOMAN SAYS PUBLIC WAS FORCED TO LEAVE CALIFORNIA FORUM OVER HER 'SAVE GIRLS SPORTS' SHIRT

"We've actually received a lot of support. I think that there's a big silent majority on this," Kevin Burns said. "I think people are afraid to speak out, but that was one of the reasons why we went down there and we held up signs."

The couple stood their ground and refused to leave.

NEW POLL SHOWS WASHINGTON STATE VOTERS ARE READY TO END BOYS COMPETING IN GIRLS' SPORTS

"We got a lot of pushback showing up there. They said the signs weren't allowed. We had to leave. My wife Sarah was being very brave and did not care. And I don't think they had a legal reason to actually push us out," he recalled.

"So we ended up actually staying there and holding our signs, and it gave the girls a boost of self-esteem. And we had a lot of parents coming up and saying, thank you for doing this. I was, I wanted to do this also. So this is kind of the start, I think."

Her mother laid bare what is at stake: "I want to stand up for girls that need someone to stand up for them."

Kevin also pressed political leaders to take up the cause, arguing that defending female athletics bridges partisan divides.

"This is a big issue that most Americans on both sides of the political aisle agree with. And I don't know why, party members, especially on the right, aren't grabbing this more and pushing it.

"I know they have in the past, but this is such a winning issue," he said. "We have friends on both sides of the aisle that agree with the girls' rights to not have to compete against boys."

The adults in charge won't do their jobs, so high school girls are doing it for them. Welcome to high school sports in 2026.

item.title: Tension erupts during House midterm debate as Lawler fact-checks New York Democrat opponent on immigration
item.description: Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., and Democrat Cait Conley clashed over ICE enforcement and New York sanctuary laws in a fiery debate that could decide House control in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., faced off against Democrat opponent Cait Conley Wednesday night in a one-hour debate filled with interruptions and fiery accusations less than three weeks before Election Day.

Lawler is vying for a third term representing New York's 17th Congressional District, a politically moderate area in the New York City suburbs that could decide the fate of who controls the House of Representatives for the final years of President Donald Trump's term.

Lawler called out Conley for misrepresenting his voting record, Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act and her own stance on immigration enforcement. Conley, meanwhile, tried to paint Lawler as a Trump acolyte who put the needs of Washington Republicans ahead of the people of his district.

Their most heated clashes came on the immigration front, when the moderator referenced the recent shooting of an illegal immigrant by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents last week in New York City while the man's 5-year-old child was in the car.

DEM CANDIDATE CLEARS CROWDED FIELD TO FACE TRUMP-BACKED INCUMBENT IN NY

"I believe that border security is national security and that we do need immigration enforcement to ensure that violent criminals and drug cartels and human traffickers and terrorist organizations aren't in our communities and that they are deported," Conley said. 

"But what we are seeing right now with the conduct of ICE is posing a public safety hazard. To your point, last week, they shot into a car where there was a 5-year-old child. I'll tell you, as a law enforcement officer, you're not permitted to do that kind of stuff."

NEW YORK GOVERNOR DEBATE HEATS UP AS BLAKEMAN, HOCHUL SPAR OVER TRUMP, SANCTUARY STATUS, ICE SHOOTING

Lawler, however, pointed out the man has a lengthy criminal rap sheet and was seen by some as a danger to his community. He also argued the shooting would never have happened had local law enforcement not been barred from handing him over to ICE by New York's sanctuary laws.

He said Conley "supports making New York a sanctuary state, prohibits cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration officials."

WATCH: LAWLER UNLOADS ON RASKIN AFTER FIERY IMMIGRATION HEARING: ‘GROW THE F--- UP’

Lawler later pivoted the discussion to Sheridan Gorman, the college student from his district who was killed while out with her friends near her campus in Chicago earlier this year. The illegal immigrant accused of killing her was previously charged with shoplifting, but Chicago sanctuary laws prevent local law enforcement from handing him over to ICE.

Conley called Gorman's death "an atrocious crime" while repeatedly pointing out it took place in Chicago.

Lawler attempted to intervene multiple times to call it "preventable," to which an irate Conley responded, "Can I finish?"

"And I do support federal agents and federal law enforcement, federal immigration enforcement, making sure that we deport violent citizens," she said.

DHS BOSS REVEALS OVAL OFFICE PLAN TO 'WITHHOLD FUNDING' FROM SANCTUARY CITIES AFTER AGGRESSIVE NEW YORK BUST

Lawler then argued, however, that Conley's support of sanctuary policies runs counter to that.

"If you think he should have been deported when he was arrested for shoplifting, he should have been turned over to ICE. Under the new law that you support, he will not be turned over to ICE, and he will be released under cashless bail," Lawler said.

It prompted the moderator to step in, telling Lawler there was no "cross-examination round."

Elsewhere in the debate, Lawler accused Conley of having "literally just lied" that Lawler voted with Trump "100% of the time."

10 DEMOCRAT-HELD HOUSE SEATS REPUBLICANS COULD FLIP TO SAVE THEIR MAJORITY

"I've been rated the third most independent member of my conference. And I have taken on the president on numerous issues, including lifting the cap on SALT, including extending Haitian TPS, including passing an extension for the ACA enhanced premium tax credit despite his objections," Lawler said.

Earlier in the debate, Conley tried to accuse Lawler of supporting tax breaks for companies that build data centers as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill.

Lawler shot back, "I know you just moved here from Virginia, so it's hard for you to understand the local communities, but the fact is ... the provision you referenced in the Working Families Tax Cut Act is $80 billion for 100% expensing for every business in America to expense plant, property and equipment. 

"Are you against our small businesses in the Hudson Valley being able to expense their plant, property and equipment and hire more people? Your attack on that rings hollow. You clearly don't understand what's actually in the tax bill. And part of the problem is you don't pay property taxes."

Amid the drama were moments of civility.

Both candidates shook hands after their spirited debate and thanked each other for appearing. Lawler also thanked Conley for her military service.

The district is a pivotal one for control of the House next year. Lawler is one of three House Republicans who won a district that former Vice President Kamala Harris also won in 2024. 

And in an election that's expected to be brutal for the GOP, both sides are pouring millions of dollars into the fight.

item.title: FBI arrest leads to maximum 90-year sentence for gymnastics coach who recorded minors at Mississippi gym
item.description: Sean Gardner received the maximum 90-year prison sentence for placing a hidden camera to record young gymnasts undressing at a Mississippi gym.
item.content:encoded:
Sean Gardner, a once prominent youth gymnastics coach, was sentenced to 90 years in prison on Wednesday after being found guilty of secretly recording young female students undressing and using the bathroom at a Mississippi gym.

Gardner’s sentence was the maximum possible span that U.S. District Judge Kristi Johnson could issue.

Gardner was ordered to serve 30 years in prison for each of the three federal child pornography production charges, which he pleaded guilty to.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The 39-year-old was arrested by the FBI last summer, which was first reported by the Associated Press. The charges against Gardner sent a shock wave through the sport, as U.S. gymnastics came under fire after another instance where its athletes were not protected enough from sexual abuse.

The most well-known case was Larry Nassar’s conviction, where he was found guilty of sexually assaulting at least 265 young women and girls during a 22-year period, which included many Olympic and U.S. women’s national gymnasts.

OKLAHOMA WINS NCAA WOMEN'S GYMNASTICS CHAMPIONSHIP FOR FOURTH TIME IN FIVE YEARS

In Gardner’s case, he pleaded guilty to placing a hidden camera in a bathroom at a gymnastics studio in Purvis, Mississippi, between December 2017 and April 2018, where he would record his students.

An investigation found that Gardner created videos with close-up images of at least 10 minors naked or undressing. Investigators found the videos on his computers years later while looking into claims that he was sexually abusing gymnasts in Iowa.

Some of Gardner’s former students at Chow’s Gymnastics and Dance Institute in West Des Moines, Iowa, claimed he used his position to prey on them, citing so in police reports and civil lawsuits.

Gardner was a key coach for top youth gymnasts that would frequent the institute founded by Liang "Chow" Qiao, another prominent coach known for producing Olympic talent.

Gardner has not yet been charged in connection with the Iowa claims, though authorities noted they would be waiting for the results of the federal case before determining how to proceed.

Some of the women involved in Gardner’s federal case also argued that USA Gymnastics and the U.S. Center for SafeSport were notified of his behavior in 2017. However, they claim the organizations failed to take action to remove him from the sport for years.

In 2022, Gardner was suspended after a gymnast at Chow’s accused him of sexual abuse. Chow later fired him.

SafeSport did its own investigation at the time, noting that Chow and other coaches were made aware of the allegations of sexual misconduct against Gardner. But they failed to report them to SafeSport, which is required by policy.

Other lawsuits still remain against Gardner, USA Gymnastics and Chow’s Gymnastics.

item.title: White House punches back at Chicago Mayor Johnson over reparations demands
item.description: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson alleged Trump enriched the ultra-rich while ignoring descendants of the formerly enslaved, drawing a White House rebuke.
item.content:encoded:
The White House punched back at Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson Wednesday after the progressive mayor claimed President Donald Trump neglected compensation for descendants of formerly enslaved Black Americans while favoring the wealthy.

Johnson appeared on the "Native Land Pod" podcast Sunday to discuss his administration's crime reduction efforts in Chicago, where violent crime rates have fallen sharply, according to the Johnson administration and Chicago Police Department data.

Speaking with hosts Angela Rye, Bakari Sellers and Andrew Gillum, Johnson argued that public safety "has to be something more than just policing," highlighting city investments in "mental behavioral healthcare, promoting detectives and expanding and investing in CVI (community violence intervention)."

REPARATIONS ACTIVISTS CALL OUT BLUE STATES FOR USING SLAVERY HISTORY TO FUND BROADER AGENDA

The podcast hosts turned to a recent Truth Social post by Trump targeting Illinois leadership over crime.

"Chicago is suffering an unprecedented and particularly violent crime wave that is getting worse by the day," Trump posted on Oct. 6. "The Federal Government can extinguish it quickly and completely, but the Mayor of Chicago, or the Governor of Illinois, must ask for our help. What is wrong with them? Why aren’t they asking? TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE! President DJT."

Johnson pushed back against the president’s statement, alleging Trump enriched wealthy Americans while ignoring the demands of "descendants of the formerly enslaved."

"He's so sorry. It's real pathetic, right, because it's so disingenuous. … This is the president who just released the largest upward transfer of wealth into the hands of the ultrarich at the expense of the demands of those of us who are descendants of the formerly enslaved," Johnson said.

"The largest upward transfer of wealth at the expense of education, housing, health care, transportation, good-paying jobs, which literally were all the demands of the formerly enslaved."

TRUMP ADMIN VOWS TO STOP REPARATIONS PROGRAMS, ACCUSES OFFICIALS OF 'VIRTUE SIGNALING' TO GET 'VOTES'

Johnson also said Trump "cut [the] violence prevention budget by $800 million," slamming the president for being concerned "about the wrong borders" as illegal weapons pour into Chicago.

"He cut the ATF budget by 30%. My local police department has worked in tandem with the AFT to get illegal weapons off the streets of Chicago. This year alone, we have removed almost 9,000 illegal weapons off the street."

The White House dismissed Johnson's claims and called on the mayor to focus on local public safety.

"Government programs that dole out money based on race are illegal," a White House spokesperson told Fox News Digital Wednesday. "Chicago would be better served if Mayor Johnson focused more on lowering his city’s homicide rate instead of advocating for divisive, unconstitutional government action." 

BLACK CHICAGOANS CALL ON REPARATIONS FROM GOVERNMENT, MONEY DEPOSITS LIKE 'STIMULUS' CHECKS

According to the mayor's office, Chicago has seen notable drops in violent crime since Johnson took office in May 2023, including double-digit decreases in homicides, shootings and overall violent crime. 

Chicago has "achieved historic double-digit decreases in crime and violence" in 2025, a spokesperson for Johnson told Fox News Digital, and is on track to see even further decreases in violent crime in 2026, with homicides down 3.8%, shootings down 1.3%and robberies down 20.9% from the same period last year.

While Johnson did not explicitly use the word "reparations" during the interview, a spokesperson pointed Fox News Digital to the city’s reparations initiatives.

Johnson previously signed an executive order establishing a 40-member reparations task force intended to address "historical harms committed against Black Chicagoans and their ancestors."

In March, Johnson announced the Repair Chicago public engagement initiative aimed at gathering lived experiences from Black residents to inform future municipal policy and direct equity measures.

The push for reparations in the region comes as the federal government ramps up legal scrutiny of local programs. Nearby Evanston, Illinois, launched a first-of-its-kind reparations program in 2021, offering $25,000 grants to eligible Black residents or their direct descendants for housing and home repairs, funded by local taxes on legal recreational marijuana sales.

To date, Evanston has distributed more than $7 million of an allotted $20 million fund. Earlier this year, the city's Reparations Committee cleared an additional wave of funding for 44 residents.

However, the Trump administration’s Department of Justice (DOJ) has signaled plans to challenge race-conscious distribution models. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division previously told Fox News Digital that local officials pushing these measures are "virtue signaling" to win votes.

CHICAGO REPARATIONS ADVOCATES SAY FEDERAL GOV MORALLY OWES '7 QUADRILLION DOLLARS' IN SLAVE LABOR

Federal intervention is expanding elsewhere as well. In September last year, the DOJ warned officials in Buncombe County, North Carolina, that it would investigate potential civil rights violations if local leaders approved recommendations from the Asheville-Buncombe Community Reparations Commission.

Responding to Johnson's remarks on the podcast, White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster emphasized that the administration remains committed to dismantling race-based initiatives.

"President Trump was resoundingly elected with a mandate to end divisive, racist policies and restore merit and efficiency," Schuster told Fox News Digital. 

"DEI ran rampant during the Biden administration, and Americans ultimately paid the price for these destructive policies with a restricted labor pool, higher operational costs and workforce inefficiencies. The Trump administration will always promote equal treatment under the law for every American, regardless of race or ethnicity."

item.title: Canadian singer Joni Mitchell officially becomes American citizen after 62-year journey
item.description: Joni Mitchell shared a photo and video from her naturalization ceremony, becoming a U.S. citizen at 82 while retaining Canadian citizenship.
item.content:encoded:
Joni Mitchell has officially become an American citizen at age 82, more than six decades after she first moved to the United States.

The music icon, who hails from Canada, announced the news on Instagram, sharing a photo of herself beaming while holding an American flag along with a video from her naturalization ceremony.

"A journey that began 62 years ago," Mitchell wrote in the caption of her post.

ART GARFUNKEL JOINS GROWING LIST OF CELEBRITIES CONSIDERING A MOVE ABROAD OVER TRUMP PRESIDENCY

Mitchell wore a red and navy blue floral cardigan that had an American flag pin along with a red beaded necklace, a red beret and black pants with black boots while posing in between an American flag and a Department of Homeland Security flag.

In the video Mitchell uploaded, she was seated in the front row at the ceremony as the speaker announced, "And Joni Mitchell, Canada" to cheers and applause from the audience.

According to KSL, Mitchell will also retain her Canadian citizenship because the U.S. and Canada legally permit dual citizenship.

The legendary singer-songwriter was born Roberta Joan Anderson in Fort Macleod, Alberta, to Royal Canadian Air Force flight Lt. William Andrew Anderson and teacher Myrtle Marguerite.

Mitchell's family lived on several bases during World War II before eventually settling in Saskatoon, which the singer has often referred to as her hometown. She went on to attend the Alberta College of Art in Calgary before dropping out and relocating to Toronto, where she played gigs at coffee houses and folk clubs.

The "Both Sides Now" songstress moved to the United States in 1965 at age 21 after marrying American folk singer Chuck Mitchell. The former couple, who lived in Detroit, Michigan, performed together as a folk duo before divorcing in 1967.

After their divorce, Mitchell left Detroit and moved to New York City, where she became part of the Greenwich Village folk scene and performed along the East Coast.

By 1968, Mitchell moved to Los Angeles, settling in Laurel Canyon, which was becoming a hub for singer-songwriters including David Crosby, Graham Nash and others. In the mid-1970s, Mitchell moved to LA's Bel Air neighborhood, where she lived in a historic 1920s home for decades.

Mitchell built her legendary music career while living in California, where she recorded many of her most acclaimed albums, including "Blue," "Court and Spark" and "Ladies of the Canyon." 

Mitchell has won 11 Grammy Awards and was inducted into both the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1997.

She was also recognized with the Kennedy Center Honors in 2021 and received the prestigious Library of Congress Gershwin Prize for Popular Song in 2023.

The musician lives in Santa Barbara, California.

Mitchell is an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump and expressed frustration that she couldn't vote in U.S. elections because she was Canadian.

CHRIS ROBINSON, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN FACE BACKLASH AS 'AMERICANS HAVE HAD ENOUGH' OF BEING LECTURED: EXPERT

During a performance at the Hollywood Bowl in LA in October 2024, Mitchell slammed Trump while performing her 1985 song "Dog Eat Dog," according to Billboard.

After singing a lyric about wealthy financiers, she added, "Like Donald Trump!"

Following her performance of the song, Mitchell responded to an audience member who shouted an anti-Trump remark.

"'F--- Donald Trump.' I love that song," she said, apparently referencing rapper YG's 2016 protest song "FDT (F--- Donald Trump)" featuring the late rapper and activist Nipsey Hussle.

She then encouraged Americans to participate in the 2024 U.S. presidential election, in which Trump ran against Democratic nominee former Vice President Kamala Harris.

"Everybody get out and vote. This is an important one. I wish I could vote . I'm Canadian. I'm one of those lousy immigrants," Mitchell said.

Months before becoming an American citizen, Mitchell criticized the political climate in the U.S. while accepting a lifetime achievement award at Canada's Juno Awards in March.

At the ceremony, Mitchell praised Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, saying, "I'm so glad to be back in Canada. This man is a blessing. You guys are so fortunate."

She also appeared to take a swipe at the Trump administration while contrasting Canada with the U.S.

"I'm living in the states, and you know what's happening there," she said.

After Mitchell's comments at the Juno Awards, the White House issued a dismissive response.

item.title: Mike Tomlin offers blunt take on NFL players-only meetings: ‘I think you’re dead’
item.description: Mike Tomlin told Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce on "New Heights" that the Dallas Cowboys' reported players-only meeting is a very troubling sign.
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys’ uneven start continued in Week 5, when they fell to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and dropped to 2-3 through five games.

Much of the scrutiny has centered on Dallas’ defense, which has struggled to find consistency during the team’s early-season stretch. Against that backdrop, the Cowboys reportedly held a players-only meeting.

Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach and current NBC Sports NFL analyst Mike Tomlin offered his perspective on what a players-only meeting can signal about a team’s state of affairs.

MIKE TOMLIN'S COACH CRITICISM MAKES HIM BETTER TV ANALYST BUT RAISES QUESTION WHETHER HE'S EYEING COWBOYS JOB

"I think you’re dead," Tomlin told ESPN’s Jason Kelce and Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce, during the latest episode of the brothers’ "New Heights" podcast.

Tomlin later clarified that his concern was less about whether a players-only meeting had occurred than about the fact that it became a subject of public discussions. "If it did occur, I’d like to not hear about it," Tomlin said. "The fact that you hear about it is what makes it BS."

JERRY JONES GOES ALL IN AS COWBOYS TRADE FOR STEELERS' JOEY PORTER JR IN HOPES OF SUPER BOWL PUSH

Jason Kelce’s visible support for the Philadelphia Eagles during broadcasts has drawn attention since he retired from the only team he played for and moved into broadcasting. Travis Kelce then asked whether Tomlin had faced criticism for speaking fondly of the Steelers during "Football Night in America" broadcasts.

"To be honest with ya, I don’t care if I do," Tomlin said. "How can you be somewhere 19 years, man, and had really a personal stake in most of the guys being there and not care for ’em? Not root for ’em? Not be for ’em? I’m not gonna pretend that I’m not. I can’t do that. Certainly, I got a job to do, and I’m gonna do it. But everybody knows where my heart is and where my support is, and I’m not apologizing for that."

Matt Eberflus served as the Cowboys’ defensive coordinator last season under head coach Brian Schottenheimer. He joined the San Francisco 49ers as assistant head coach/defense for 2026, with Dallas turning to Christian Parker to lead the defense.

The Cowboys have shown modest improvement under Parker in some areas, but they still rank near the bottom of the NFL in yards allowed per game through five weeks.

Shortly after last Thursday’s 24-16 loss to the Bucs, Schottenheimer began making changes to a Dallas defense that has largely struggled thus far. One of those changes included adding a familiar face to the coaching staff.

item.title: Trump torches Democrats at Arizona rally, warns they will ‘destroy our country’ ahead of midterms
item.description: Trump rallied for Andy Biggs in Bullhead City, blasting Dem Gov. Katie Hobbs and urging Arizona voters to turn the state red in honor of Charlie Kirk.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump brought a blunt warning to Arizona voters Wednesday, declaring Democrats would "destroy our country" as he blasted their State of the Union conduct and urged supporters to turn the state red from top to bottom.

With Election Day less than three weeks away, Trump rallied behind Rep. Andy Biggs, the Republican gubernatorial nominee, and a slate of GOP candidates during a campaign stop in Bullhead City, taking aim at Democrat Gov. Katie Hobbs and calling for a victory in honor of Charlie Kirk.

"On election night, Arizona is going to prove that America does not belong to those who hate it," Trump said. "America belongs to those who love, love, love, love — love it."

TRUMP CAMPAIGN INSIDER REVEALS STRATEGY BEHIND MIDTERM BLITZ THAT WHITE HOUSE HOPES PAYS OFF BIG

Biggs joined Trump onstage and pointed back to the president’s February State of the Union address to Congress, accusing Democrats of refusing to stand when Trump challenged lawmakers about their commitment to Americans.

"Vote Republican top to bottom," Biggs told the crowd. "Let’s turn Arizona red."

TRUMP ISSUES BLUNT MIDTERM WARNING; VANCE GREETED WITH ‘48’ CHANTS: TOP TAKEAWAYS FROM GOP CONVENTION

Trump seized on the criticism, shifting to lawmakers’ reactions to a veteran honored during the speech.

"Not one Democrat smiled or clapped," Trump said. "And that’s when I looked at them, and I said, ‘You people are crazy.’

JOHN FETTERMAN DEFENDS TRUMP SUPPORTERS, CONDEMNS FELLOW DEMOCRATS' 'F--- TRUMP' STRATEGY

"But that’s what we have," he continued. "They’ll destroy our country."

Trump’s account combined separate moments from the Feb. 24 address. He awarded the Medal of Honor to retired Navy Capt. E. Royce Williams, who was 100 at the time, as Trump recalled Wednesday. He also recognized World War II veteran George "Buddy" Taggart.

MICHAEL MONSOOR HAD AN ESCAPE ROUTE; THE MEDAL OF HONOR RECIPIENT CHOSE TO SAVE HIS TEAMMATES INSTEAD

BATTLEGROUND DEM GOVERNOR TORCHED FOR ‘DRUNKEN SAILOR’ SPENDING GOP CRITIC SAYS IS SYMBOLIC OF BIGGER PROBLEM

Trump praised Biggs’ running mate, former state Sen. Sine Kerr, who is seeking to become Arizona’s first lieutenant governor. 

Biggs selected Kerr in July for the newly created office.

TRUMP FLEXES GOP MUSCLE IN ARIZONA PRIMARIES AS DEMS DODGE FAR-LEFT UPSET

Trump also urged supporters to elect Republican secretary of state candidate Alex Kolodin, calling him "a warrior for election integrity" as he attacked Democratic incumbent Adrian Fontes.

"You look good. Central casting, actually," Trump told Kolodin, joking that he looked "a little bit nerdy."

Trump gave shoutouts to Republican Reps. Paul Gosar, Abe Hamadeh and Eli Crane, describing Hamadeh and Crane as "warriors." He also praised congressional candidate Mark Lamb, calling him "a friend of mine" and urging voters to send him to Washington to represent Arizona’s 5th Congressional District.

The rally also included a tribute to Kirk, whom Trump remembered on what he said would have been the conservative activist’s 33rd birthday.

"A great person, a great man, a great friend of mine," Trump said as the crowd chanted, "Charlie! Charlie!"

Trump offered support to Kirk’s widow, Erika, and their family before turning the remembrance into a call to vote.

"In Charlie’s honor, we want you to go out and vote," Trump said. "He’d be out there fighting like nobody else. So, let’s have a big victory in honor of Charlie Kirk."

item.title: Rogan warns Trump's voters feel betrayed by Iran war with 'no easy way out'
item.description: Joe Rogan told Michael Douglas the Iran war has infuriated President Donald Trump's voters who believed they were electing a president to prevent new conflicts.
item.content:encoded:
Podcaster Joe Rogan discussed the war in Iran with actor Michael Douglas Wednesday, arguing the conflict has angered supporters of President Donald Trump, who voted for him in part because of his promises to avoid new wars.

"I do not like this Iran war in any way, shape or form," Rogan said. "It doesn't make any sense for us. It seems like it's getting really out of hand. They were trying to get every single president, including Trump in his first term, to do this," Rogan said on his podcast.

Douglas, who is both Jewish and a pro-Israel Democrat, agreed that the conflict was a mistake.

ROGAN SAYS TRUMP ‘F---ED IT UP,’ MAY HAVE HANDED COUNTRY BACK TO THE DEMS IN 2028 WITH UNPOPULAR IRAN WAR

"Now we've done it, and it's very clear it's a giant quagmire. It's very clear there's no easy way out. Not good," Rogan said. 

"And there's still a lot of people that insist that it had to happen, that Iran was the greatest funder of state terrorism in the world and that what they were doing was, you know, funding and arming these forces and having them do these — to commit these terrorist attacks. And I'm sure a lot of that's true."

"I concur," Douglas said, noting his concern about the expansion of the conflict after an attack on an airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, which he compared to attacks on major U.S. airports. 

"I'm surprised with all of our Western intelligence and Israelis’ intelligence that we have not had a better handle on the situation."

Rogan responded to criticism that the Trump administration had been persuaded the conflict would be an easy victory, saying, "Well, look, obviously I'm not an expert on international relations, but I don't think the picture that they painted of how this was going to go down was even remotely accurate."

"Yeah," Douglas agreed. After Rogan recalled Iran’s crackdowns on protesters and mass arrests, Douglas said there have been "tens of thousands" of arrests and appeared to suggest the war was instigated by Israel.

"I think it was instigated by Israel by the fact that they had information that these key Iranian leaders would all be together and were persuaded that we take them all out. We can turn it over and, yeah, didn't turn out that way," the actor said.

"I don't know how they convinced Trump to do it," Rogan said. "I do know that in any international conflict, I'm sure even during Vietnam, even after people kind of knew the Gulf of Tonkin was horses---, there was, I'm sure there's people even today that defend the Vietnam War," Rogan said, referring to U.S. claims of an attack on the USS Maddox in the waters off Vietnam on Aug. 4, 1964, that escalated the conflict.

"You're going to get people that support this war," he continued. "But I think the majority of the United States felt like one of the things that we were voting for when we voted for Trump is, ‘No more wars.’ Stop this s---. Like, it's crazy. 

"You know, when I remember one of his speeches or one of his interviews, someone was asking him about Ukraine. ‘Do you want Ukraine to win? Do you want Russia to win?’ And he said, ‘I just want people to stop dying.’ And most people who voted for him based on that feel very upset that there's a new war going on."

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS OPPOSE THE IRAN WAR, SEE PROLONGED COMMITMENT

"Yeah, yeah," Douglas agreed.

Rogan also acknowledged that experts have warned about Iran's increasing missile production and the dangers of the country acquiring a nuclear weapon.

Trita Parsi, the co-founder and executive vice president of the Quincy Institute, spoke to Fox News Digital about Rogan’s comments.

"I fully agree that Trump's decision to start a war with Iran has deeply frustrated the anti-war component of his 2024 coalition and that it will be extremely difficult to get them back," he said. "The gap between what he so explicitly promised — no more wars — and what he has delivered — yet another war of choice in the Middle East that does not serve U.S. interests — could not be any wider."

Like Rogan and Douglas, Parsi agreed that "the Israeli presentation of Iran could not have been further from the truth, as Iran's military capabilities and the theocracy's resilience were far more formidable than the Israelis had asserted."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

He offered a grim assessment of the Republican Party’s future.

"The war has created a major rift within the Republican Party and created a MAGA vs. America First coalition," Parsi said. "Moreover, the GOP's ability to bring anti-war constituents to its side has been severely damaged. Many of them left the Democratic Party because of the wars in Ukraine and Gaza; now many of them will return to the Democratic Party due to the war in Iran.

"These voters were crucial to Trump's success in 2016 and 2024, and their significance is only likely to grow."

"What matters most to the American people is having a commander in chief who takes decisive action to eliminate threats and keep them safe, which is exactly what President Trump is doing," White House spokesperson Davis Engle told Fox News Digital.

"He campaigned proudly on his promise to deny the Iranian regime the ability to develop a nuclear weapon, and Americans are already safer because of his bold leadership," he added. 

"The president makes these incredibly important national security decisions based on the best interests of the American people."

item.title: John Stamos says Beach Boys legend Mike Love is facing 'serious health challenges'
item.description: John Stamos revealed Mike Love is facing serious health challenges, but the Beach Boys legend insisted on performing at the Ryman over the weekend.
item.content:encoded:
John Stamos performed with the Beach Boys on Sunday at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville.

Before the show, the actor was overcome with emotion talking about Beach Boys legend Mike Love, who is facing "serious health challenges."

Stamos, 63, shared a carousel of images on social media with his "musical hero and mentor" before admitting he was "struggling" to put his feelings into words.

ROD STEWART CONFIRMS FINAL TOUR AFTER HEART PROCEDURE AND HEALTH SCARES

"My beloved friend, father figure, musical hero and mentor, Mike Love, is facing serious health challenges," he wrote. "We hope he’ll be doing what he loves for years to come, but we don’t know what the future holds. We have tonight."

At Tuesday's Hot Cuisine fundraiser for the Scleroderma Research Foundation (SRF), Stamos told Fox News Digital it was his mission to get Love to the Ryman Auditorium for a performance of a lifetime.

"Our goal was to get him up at the Ryman this weekend. He wanted it," Stamos said. "I've been spending a lot of time with him, you know, quiet time. We've been listening to music. … Doo-wop. He loves Doo-Wop.

"And I said, ‘You gotta tell me, do you really think you can do these shows this weekend?’ He said, ‘Yes, and I really want to.’ I said, 'We'll make it happen.'

"Everybody told him not to — doctors, his family — but it was something he wanted to do. He's made all my dreams come true and all my wishes. So, I had to fulfill his wish, and we made sure that he got there and did a good job."

SRF presented John Stamos with the Bob Saget Legacy Award, recognizing his steadfast support for scleroderma research and his commitment to following in Bob’s footsteps by shining a spotlight on scleroderma and raising funds toward a cure.

Love's representatives did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. It's unclear what health struggles Love faces.

Stamos and Love's son, Brian Love, delivered speeches prior to the show.

"One thing about him is he's stubborn, and he's steadfast, and he did not want to miss the Ryman. I mean, for good reason," Brian said, via Variety. 

"Look at this place. So, we are happy. We're going to be positive. We're gonna sing along. But I still remember something he told me when I was a child, and it stuck with me. I said, ‘Dad, why do you do so many shows?’ I mean, we are talking about a guy who's done over 100 concerts a year well up into his 80s."

"That's just incredible, right? So, he told me, ‘Well, if you don’t do as many concerts, you don't see as many towns, and then that means less people get to hear the amazing Beach Boys personally.' So, he's always cared for the small towns, the fairs. … This is obviously a much more well-known, beautiful venue. But he cares about the listener, and I think it's such an honor to be part of that. And we've gotta live in the moment."

Stamos said, "All we have is tonight really, and I think it's going to be very, very special. Mike, he insisted on being here. … He's done over 7,000 live shows. And tonight'll be 7,422, I think exactly. I think that's where we're at. He's counting. … We love you, and have the greatest night ever, and God bless you all."

After the curtains opened, Love was already seated on stage, the outlet reported.

He sang in his seat along with his bandmates but did not do his lead vocals.

During the performance, the Beach Boys legend addressed concerns about his health, saying, "Obviously, I’ve been going through some health issues for quite a while. But I didn’t want to miss being at the Ryman with y’all."

Variety reported that Love was helped up by Brian and Stamos at the end of the show as the song "We Are The Champions" by Queen played.

JON BON JOVI ABRUPTLY ENDS MADISON SQUARE GARDEN SHOW AFTER HEALTH SETBACK

In his social media post, Stamos acknowledged that Love "is a fighter," and despite "doctors, family and friends urging him to focus on his health, he insists on being on stage."

"He says he needs his band, the audience, his friends and drummer surrounding him to lift him up," Stamos wrote. "I’ve played with Mike for 41 years. I never imagined how deeply it would affect me to see someone larger than life face something so human and fragile."

The Beach Boys have been touring in support of the 60th anniversary of their groundbreaking 11th studio album, "Pet Sounds."

Stamos noted that "the Mike Love we see tonight may not be exactly the Mike we’ve always known. But he’s still every bit the Mike we love."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"His lyrics, optimism, unforgettable hooks and more than 7,000 concerts have brought joy to generations," Stamos wrote. "What he’s given me personally is immeasurable.

"Forty-one years of stages, airplanes, hotel rooms, laughter and moments nobody else saw. He married Caitlin and me. He’s shared experiences with my family, and now my son."

The "Full House" star noted that Love didn't only give him a spot in the band. He "gave me a place in his life."

WATCH HERE: JOHN STAMOS FULFILLS BEACH BOYS LEGEND MIKE LOVE'S WISH TO PLAY IN NASHVILLE

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"He taught me how to entertain, hold a stage, connect with an audience and make people feel something. I carry those lessons everywhere," Stamos said. "He’s made me a better musician, entertainer and man.

"This life with Mike and the Beach Boys has become part of my identity. I’ve felt entrusted with being a steward of this extraordinary music, carrying it to new generations."

Stamos wanted to "be completely present" performing with Love at the Ryman over the weekend and "hear every harmony, familiar joke and cheer. Feel that first chord hit and watch age, illness and time disappear. Just a bunch of guys making music together."

He wrote, "Maybe the hardest part of loving someone is becoming so accustomed to the miracle of having them there that you forget it’s a miracle at all.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"Tonight, I won’t forget," Stamos wrote. "I want to cherish every second without feeling those seconds slipping away. That’s what I’m giving him.

"We don’t know what tomorrow brings. But we have tonight."

Fox News Digital's Larry Fink contributed to this report.

item.title: Federal agents seize phone of Rep Ilhan Omar in raid tied to immigration fraud probe
item.description: Federal agents raided Ilhan Omar's D.C. home and seized her cellphone as part of a criminal fraud investigation into her immigration paperwork.
item.content:encoded:
Federal authorities seized a cellphone belonging to Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., during a Monday raid on her Washington, D.C., home as part of a criminal fraud investigation into her immigration paperwork.

Omar's immigration history is facing renewed scrutiny, with investigators issuing more than a dozen subpoenas to her family members following the raid on her residence.

Investigators are examining whether Omar's family lied about her age when she immigrated to the United States in 1995. Omar became a naturalized U.S. citizen in 2000. The probe centers on whether the age listed on her application differed from her actual birth date.

WATCH: ILHAN OMAR DENIES FEDS HAVE CONTACTED HER AFTER BORDER CZAR HOMAN CONFIRMS 'CRIMINAL' INVESTIGATION

She was reported as 17 years old at the time she acquired citizenship, making her eligible to receive citizenship automatically through her father's naturalization.

Questions surrounding Omar's age resurfaced after her congressional staff contacted a Minnesota public library months after she took office to request that her birth year in historical records be changed from 1981 to 1982.

HOMAN CONFIRMS 'CRIMINAL' INVESTIGATION INVOLVING ILHAN OMAR, SAYS HE KNOWS 'THINGS ARE GOING ON’

Omar’s husband, Tim Mynett, expressed confidence when asked about the investigation into his wife.

"My wife came here when she was 12 years old as a child war refugee," Mynett told Fox News Digital this week. "No concerns."

ILHAN OMAR’S EMBATTLED HUSBAND APPEARS AT SCENE OF HSI RAID IN MIDST OF CRIMINAL FRAUD INVESTIGATION

Authorities are also examining paperwork submitted by Omar's late father, Nur Omar Mohamed, regarding his application to enter the U.S., investigating whether statements on his filings were untruthful.

Omar has denied any wrongdoing and accused the Trump administration of weaponizing federal law enforcement against political opponents.

DEMOCRATS HAVE ‘DIRTY HANDS’ OVER COMPLAINTS ABOUT OMAR RAID WEEKS BEFORE ELECTION, EX-PROSECUTOR SAYS

"For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back," her office said in a statement. "Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid. The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong. No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies."

In addition to the immigration probe, a separate inquiry is underway regarding Omar's federal financial disclosures. Officials noted that financial disclosure review is unrelated to the raid on her home.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Omar's office.

Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price contributed to this report.

item.title: Major airline abandons 3 key cities as passengers face shrinking flight choices
item.description: After all three routes failed to meet performance expectations, American Airlines has dropped nonstop flights to Santa Maria, Tijuana and Doha this year.
item.content:encoded:
American Airlines has dropped flights to three destinations across the U.S., Mexico and the Middle East this year, leaving some travelers with fewer flight options.

The airline has discontinued service to Santa Maria, California; Tijuana, Mexico; and Doha, Qatar, according to aviation outlet Simple Flying, which cited data from aviation analytics company Cirium.

The cuts have left Santa Maria without service from a major U.S. legacy carrier, while Tijuana lost its only nonstop route operated by a U.S. airline.

FURIOUS CROWDS PROTEST SKY-HIGH HOUSING COSTS AND MASS TOURISM IN MAJOR CITY

By cutting its routes from Phoenix to Santa Maria and Tijuana, American Airlines has exited both destinations.

At Santa Maria, Allegiant Air remains the only commercial airline serving the airport, with flights to Las Vegas, according to Simple Flying.

Meanwhile, Qatar Airways has taken over the Philadelphia-to-Doha route, restoring nonstop service between the two cities after American's departure.

Regarding the cancellation of service to Santa Maria, American Airlines said the decision was based on performance.

American Airlines operated service to Santa Maria, California, under its American Eagle brand through a partnership with SkyWest Airlines, a spokesperson from the company told local outlet KEYT earlier this year.

INNOCENT MISTAKE ON LONG FLIGHT COULD HAVE DEVASTATING CONSEQUENCES FOR TRAVELERS

"Unfortunately, flights to SMX did not meet performance expectations, and SkyWest informed American it will discontinue service as of May 7," the official said.

In June, American Airlines permanently cut its Philadelphia-to-Doha route after previously suspending flights due to regional hostilities, according to The Philadelphia Inquirer.

"As part of an optimization of our network and fleet, American has made the difficult decision to discontinue service to Doha, Qatar (DOH)," American Airlines spokesperson Bri Harper said in a statement to the outlet. 

In August, American Airlines discontinued service to Tijuana, Mexico, after the route failed to meet performance expectations.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

American Airlines routinely reviews its routes to ensure "optimal deployment of aircraft," a spokesperson told aviation outlet AirlineGeeks, adding that service to Tijuana had not met "performance expectations."

Fox News Digital reached out to American Airlines for further comment.

Steven Arroyo, an aviation safety expert and retired United Airlines captain based in Florida, told Fox News Digital that route cancellations are a common part of the airline business.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"If airlines are consistently not making money on a route, they're going to pull out, and it happens all the time," Arroyo said. "It's part of the economic reality of running an airline efficiently."

Arroyo said travelers should monitor routes and ticket prices when planning upcoming trips.

He encouraged travelers to "keep an eye on what's going on" with their planned routes and "do a little bit of research" before booking their trips.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Arroyo also urged travelers planning trips to the Middle East to closely monitor their flights and consider backup arrangements.

"If you are traveling to the Middle East, to the Gulf region, I would highly advise all passengers, all customers, to keep a careful watch," he said.

"Go on the internet. Go to the company's website. See what's going on. ... Try to lock in those prices or make alternative plans if it looks like flights may be canceled on your route."

item.title: Netflix greenlights doc on Daejon Love, the fake 49ers WR who fleeced dating app victims for $1.3M
item.description: Netflix's "Untold: Wide Deceiver" explores how Daejon Love used dating apps and fake 49ers workouts to swindle women out of over $1.3 million.
item.content:encoded:
Netflix has officially ordered an Untold documentary on the wildest fake-baller scheme in modern sports, locking in on Daejon Love, the 35-year-old con man who swindled women out of more than $1.3 million by pretending to be a San Francisco 49ers wide receiver.

Titled "Untold: Wide Deceiver," the documentary will focus on the bizarre workings of Love's scam and feature interviews with the victims who bought into the scheme.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Federal prosecutors say Love and his 18-year-old accomplice, Taylor Jamie Chan, used Tinder, Bumble, Hinge and Facebook Dating to target women across California, Oregon and Washington.

MAN ACCUSED OF POSING AS 49ERS PLAYER IN $1.3M ROMANCE SCAM APPEARED IN VIDEO OBTAINED BY OUTKICK

Love went full method actor to concoct his ruse. To convince women he was catching passes on Sundays, he staged entire fake workouts, including clips of himself running routes on public beaches while wearing a replica 49ers helmet.

The facade collapsed in August when the FBI arrested Love and Chan at an airport in Boise, Idaho. Love was indicted on federal conspiracy and wire fraud charges, with the FBI identifying dozens of victims across multiple states.

LESEAN MCCOY THROWS HIS SUPPORT BEHIND THE GUY WHO ALLEGEDLY SCAMMED WOMEN BY POSING AS A 49ERS PLAYER

In one video, Love staged a mock contract signing, flashing team gear and telling the camera, "Niners, you already know, Niner gang."

When questioned about his status on the active roster, Love's go-to excuse was pointing to an allegedly injured finger.

In one Instagram video, he flashed an AI-generated Google search snippet that erroneously listed him as a Niners receiver, telling his followers, "That's Google. That's not me, that's Google."

Once he convinced them he was an NFL star and real estate player, he pressured them to take out high-interest personal loans to fund his fake, high-yield investment programs.

WOMAN LOSES NEARLY $1M IN LINKEDIN ROMANCE SCAM

None of the money was ever invested.

Love burned through the cash on luxury cars, designer jewelry, and flashy vacations to keep up the appearance of wealth for his next target.

Once a victim ran out of cash or started asking basic financial questions, Love cut off all contact. He pleaded not guilty and remains held without bail ahead of a federal jury trial set for Dec. 15.
